title: DVI-DTM: Dual-View Representation Learning for Interpretable Short Text Dynamic Topic Modeling
subcategory: short-text dynamic topic model with LLM agents
task: Dynamic (temporal) topic modelling of short texts with human-readable topic descriptions
problem: Semantic ambiguity (sparse short texts, temporal semantic shift) and interpretation ambiguity (topics without human-understandable descriptions).
architecture: Dual-View Representation Learning aligns a sentence view (trainable SBERT encoder) and a temporal-aware term view (frozen PLM term embeddings passed through a Temporal Term Encoder: multi-head self-attention with term and time positional encodings); a GEA Topic Refiner of three LLM agents (Generator, Evaluator, Assigner) writes topic descriptions and refines document-topic assignments; Dual-Factor Ranking (semantic relevance + temporal uniqueness) selects evolving topic terms.
llm_or_encoder: all-mpnet-base-v2 SBERT; LLM agents: Qwen3-max, DeepSeek-R1, GPT-4o, GPT-5
key_results: StackOverflow (GPT-5 agents): Purity 0.545, NMI 0.482, NPMI 0.290, C_V 0.620, TD 1.000, TTC 0.581.
Average gains over baselines: 5.5% Purity and 3.2% NMI; over dynamic baselines 3.0% NPMI, 7.0% C_V, 4.1% TD and 8.5% TTC.
strengths: Addresses both sparsity and interpretability of short-text dynamic topics.
Ablation shows the model stays competitive without the LLM refiner.

limitations.text: Depends on large LLMs in the refiner; smaller open models (e.g. Llama-3-8B) may fail to generate discriminative topic descriptions.
Generated topics may reflect biases present in the real-world datasets.

notes: K = 20 topics, averages over five runs; T-test significance reported.
